curve.Spike: Peaks Ancient-Classical. Bonus is loudest before turn ~100.
curve.Ramp: Peaks Medieval-Renaissance. Needs a functional early game to reach it.
curve.Bloom: Peaks Industrial onward. Near-inert early; needs a survival plan, not a growth plan.
curve.Flat: Compounds evenly across the whole game. No cliff, no dead zone.

conversion.Permanent: The peak banks into something that persists after the bonus stops mattering (cities, wonders, districts, banked civics).
conversion.Conditional: Persists only while an external state holds (war footing, suzerainty, amenity level, someone else's golden age).
conversion.Expiring: Runs on a timer or a trigger. If it didn't buy territory inside the window, there is no second act.

schema.condition_cost: What the kit charges you in exchange. 'None' means the bonus is free.
schema.convert_by: For Spike leaders: the rough turn by which the tempo must have become permanent assets. Null where not applicable.

leaders.name: Gilgamesh
leaders.condition_cost: None
leaders.note: War-Carts expire as units but captured cities do not. Cleanest spike on the roster.

leaders.name: Amanitore
leaders.condition_cost: Nubian Pyramids want desert-adjacent placement
leaders.note: Dual-banks: conquest AND permanently cheaper districts. Survives its own spike better than most.

leaders.name: Montezuma
leaders.condition_cost: Combat strength scales with luxury variety, so needs wide territory
leaders.note: Captured Builders are permanent infrastructure. Luxury bonus decays in relevance as strength numbers inflate.

leaders.name: Tomyris
leaders.condition_cost: None
leaders.note: Highest-risk spike. Duplicate units and heal-on-kill produce zero standing yield. Pure tempo.

leaders.name: Simon Bolivar
leaders.condition_cost: None
leaders.note: Movement applies to civilians, so it compounds settling speed as much as war speed.

leaders.name: Alexander
leaders.condition_cost: Must stay at war to keep the engine running
leaders.note: No war weariness is only worth anything while at war. Peace turns the kit off.

leaders.name: Gorgo
leaders.condition_cost: Requires a continuous supply of things to kill
leaders.note: Culture banks into unlocked civics permanently, which is why she outlasts other combat-trigger leaders.

leaders.name: Ambiorix
leaders.condition_cost: Bonus only holds while units stay clustered
leaders.note: Positioning discipline is the cost. Falls apart in wide-front late-game wars.

leaders.name: Shaka
leaders.condition_cost: Genuinely weak until Mercenaries
leaders.note: Auto-upgrade on capture is a compounding loop, not a flat bonus. Strongest ramp in the category.

leaders.name: Cyrus
leaders.condition_cost: Surprise War diplomatic and grievance penalties
leaders.note: Ten-turn window, repeatable but never banked. The trap case for the whole Spike tier.

leaders.name: Genghis Khan
leaders.condition_cost: Requires trade route setup before each target
leaders.note: Captured cavalry is real accumulation. The visibility bonus is a setup tax, not a restriction.

leaders.name: Chandragupta
leaders.condition_cost: Only fires on Wars of Territorial Expansion, so needs an adjacent target
leaders.note: Doubly gated: right war type AND inside the timer.

leaders.name: Harald Hardrada
leaders.condition_cost: Coastal-heavy map dependency
leaders.note: Pillage yield is one-time per tile. Raiding is income, not territory, so nothing accumulates structurally.

leaders.name: Matthias Corvinus
leaders.condition_cost: Ongoing gold and envoy spend; levied units are rented, not owned
leaders.note: Captured cities are permanent but the army itself never is. Cash flow is the whole constraint.

leaders.name: Suleiman
leaders.condition_cost: Nothing early, which is also the problem
leaders.note: No meaningful Ancient-era identity. Needs a survival plan for the first 100 turns.

leaders.name: Lautaro
leaders.condition_cost: Depends entirely on other civs entering Golden Ages
leaders.note: Only leader whose trigger is owned by someone else. Reactive by design.

leaders.name: Trajan
leaders.condition_cost: None
leaders.note: Free Monument in every city is the definition of a compounding, unconditional bonus. Beginner-safe.

leaders.name: Hojo Tokimune
leaders.condition_cost: Tight city spacing; rewards planning discipline
leaders.note: Terrain-agnostic, which is rare. Works on almost any start. Beginner-safe.

leaders.name: Qin Shi Huang
leaders.condition_cost: Builder charges spent on wonders are charges not spent on improvements
leaders.note: Wonders are the most permanent asset in the game. Best conversion rate of any spike.

leaders.name: Frederick Barbarossa
leaders.condition_cost: Extra district needs population and production to actually fill
leaders.note: The district cap break compounds with every city founded. Scales with empire size, not era.

leaders.name: Pachacuti
leaders.condition_cost: Mountain terrain dependency; dead start without it
leaders.note: Turns the map's worst tiles into workable ones. Highest start-roll variance on the roster.

leaders.name: John Curtin
leaders.condition_cost: Requires being attacked, which you do not control
leaders.note: Ten-turn production bursts. Banks only if the burst is spent on something permanent.

leaders.name: Victoria (Age of Steam)
leaders.condition_cost: Iron and coal access; percentage bonuses need an existing base to multiply
leaders.note: Textbook Bloom. Multiplicative bonuses on a small early empire are near-zero.

leaders.name: Ba Trieu
leaders.condition_cost: Districts only on Woods, Rainforest, or Marsh. Severe placement restriction.
leaders.note: Highest condition cost in the game. The restriction never lifts.

leaders.name: Lady Six Sky
leaders.condition_cost: Hard 6-tile expansion ceiling; penalties outside it
leaders.note: Flat but capped. Yields compound, empire size does not. Trades scale for efficiency.

leaders.name: Nzinga Mbande
leaders.condition_cost: Continent-locked; overseas cities are actively bad
leaders.note: Same shape as Lady Six Sky but the ceiling is drawn by the map instead of a radius.

leaders.name: Seondeok
leaders.condition_cost: Seowon isolation forfeits all district adjacency stacking
leaders.note: Trades ceiling for floor. Guaranteed science on any start, but cannot be optimized upward.

leaders.name: Hammurabi
leaders.condition_cost: Base per-turn Science permanently halved
leaders.note: The halving never goes away. Eureka availability thins in later eras, so the engine quietly dies.

leaders.name: Robert the Bruce
leaders.condition_cost: Permanent Ecstatic amenity upkeep across the whole empire
leaders.note: The bonus is rented every single turn. One luxury loss switches it off empire-wide.

leaders.name: Teddy Roosevelt (Bull Moose)
leaders.condition_cost: Cannot chop; forfeits the standard production-acceleration lever
leaders.note: Appeal is a permanent tile property, so the yields never decay.

leaders.name: Kupe
leaders.condition_cost: No chopping, plus an ocean start with no immediate settle
leaders.note: Pays a real opening tempo cost before the ramp begins.

leaders.name: Pericles
leaders.condition_cost: Ongoing envoy investment; suzerainty can be taken from you
leaders.note: Flat and smooth, but rented. Losing suzerainty is an instant global culture cut.

leaders.name: Cleopatra (Ptolemaic)
leaders.condition_cost: River and floodplain dependency
leaders.note: Appeal inversion pays early in Food and late in National Parks. Genuinely two-phase.

leaders.name: Pedro II
leaders.condition_cost: Rainforest dependency; must not clear it
leaders.note: Great People refunds compound. Every recruit makes the next one cheaper in real terms.

leaders.name: Ludwig II
leaders.condition_cost: Requires deliberately leaving Wonders unfinished, locking up production
leaders.note: The bonus ends the moment the wonder completes. Uniquely self-terminating.

leaders.name: Kristina
leaders.condition_cost: None mechanically, but no early-game identity at all
leaders.note: Auto-theming is pure late-game convenience. Needs a survival plan for the first 80 turns.

leaders.name: Catherine de Medici (Black Queen)
leaders.condition_cost: None
leaders.note: Rare kit that pays in every era for a different reason: spy, then combat visibility, then tourism.

leaders.name: Wilfrid Laurier
leaders.condition_cost: Tundra start; the terrain bonus is survival, not growth
leaders.note: Surprise War immunity is the survival plan built into the kit. Cleanest Bloom on the roster.

leaders.name: Eleanor of Aquitaine
leaders.condition_cost: Needs a large Great Work stockpile before anything happens
leaders.note: Annexed cities are permanent, but the prerequisite is a long build-up with nothing to show.

leaders.name: Peter
leaders.condition_cost: Tundra dependency
leaders.note: Great Writers and Artists are permanent assets. Turns dead terrain into a Great Person engine.

leaders.name: Jayavarman VII
leaders.condition_cost: River dependency
leaders.note: Food, Housing, and Faith from one district. Compounds through population, so it never plateaus.

leaders.name: Saladin
leaders.condition_cost: None
leaders.note: The guaranteed religion is what lets him skip the early Faith race entirely. Free tempo.

leaders.name: Gandhi
leaders.condition_cost: Must stay at peace; scales with other civs founding religions
leaders.note: Output partly determined by other players' choices. Second-most externally dependent after Lautaro.

leaders.name: Menelik II
leaders.condition_cost: Hill settling requirement
leaders.note: Faith-to-Science-and-Culture conversion means one yield stream funds three victory paths.

leaders.name: Gitarja
leaders.condition_cost: Water-heavy map required; dead on continents
leaders.note: Highest map-roll dependency in the Faith category.

leaders.name: Jadwiga
leaders.condition_cost: Guaranteed diplomatic hostility from every neighbor
leaders.note: Stolen tiles and converted cities are permanent. The cost is paid in grievances, not mechanics.

leaders.name: Basil II
leaders.condition_cost: Requires founding a religion AND spreading it to the target first
leaders.note: Two-step prerequisite before the combat bonus exists. Slow to come online, brutal once it does.

leaders.name: Philip II
leaders.condition_cost: Bonus only applies against differently-faithed civs
leaders.note: If a neighbor converts to your religion, your combat bonus against them evaporates.

leaders.name: Tamar
leaders.condition_cost: Envoy and wall investment; Golden Age chain breaks if an era is missed
leaders.note: Chained bonuses are fragile. One Normal Age resets the whole compounding sequence.

leaders.name: Mansa Musa
leaders.condition_cost: Severe Production penalty and desert dependency
leaders.note: Buys permanence with gold instead of building it. Works, but only if the gold never stops.

leaders.name: Yongle
leaders.condition_cost: Project turns spent reaching pop thresholds are turns not spent building
leaders.note: Threshold-gated rather than gradual. Nothing happens, then everything does.

leaders.name: Dido
leaders.condition_cost: Coastal settling; capital relocation has a real opportunity cost
leaders.note: Loyalty immunity removes the single biggest constraint on overseas expansion.

leaders.name: Tokugawa
leaders.condition_cost: International trade heavily penalized; forfeits foreign trade income entirely
leaders.note: Trades a whole mechanic away for a stronger version of a different one.

leaders.name: Joao III
leaders.condition_cost: Water map plus coastal foreign cities that must actually exist and stay reachable
leaders.note: Routes depend on other civs' city placement. Yields drop if targets are lost or conquered.
